reason: The food remainder contains plant fibre that the resident microbes may use, making their interaction a natural place to start.
expectation: The microbes will act on some of the undigested material in the colon.

effect: The microbes ferment some remaining fibre, producing fatty acids and gas; I will connect these contents to their colon habitat.
reaction: The reminder that some fibre remains makes the result feel more informative than a complete breakdown.
reason: The fermenting contents belong in the colon shown within the connected body, so joining them may reveal their effects on the host.
expectation: The colon will interact with the fermenting contents, possibly taking up some of their products.

alternatives.reason: The mucus may also be part of the microbes' immediate habitat.

effect: The colon takes up some microbial fatty acids as well as water and salts; the mucus remains to be connected.
reaction: The arrows make the exchange with the body clearer.
reason: The mucus belongs on the colon lining and may show how the host provides a habitat for the microbes.
expectation: The mucus will be added to the colon and reveal its relationship with the microbes.

effect: The completed colon shows mucus separating most bacteria from the lining, while water, salts and microbial fatty acids cross into the body.
reaction: The combined picture makes the relationship clearer, though the final fitting was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the food remainder with microbes was most worthwhile: it showed that bacteria ferment some fibre into fatty acids and gas, while some fibre remains.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mucus was the least engaging choice because its location was already apparent, although the result clarified its separating role.

surprise.text: I was interested that colon cells can use some of the fatty acids made by microbes and that some enter the blood.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each involved an identifiable part of the colon or its contents.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter: the microbial exchange connected digestion to the body in a way I found interesting, even though the combinations were fairly predictable.
